title: Trajectory optimizer: kernel prober for mixed-architecture & sequence-length workloads
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Introduce a runtime component (Trajectory Optimizer) that actively probes a small number of kernel execution trajectories and uses a lightweight cost model to pick a per-request execution policy. Targets mixed-architecture clusters (A100/4090/MI300) and variable sequence-length distributions where static heuristics suffer tail latency and cost inefficiencies.
background: Existing kernel-selection heuristics rely on offline profiles and broad seq-len buckets. We observe 95th/99th tail regressions on mixed loads where prefill-heavy conversational requests are interleaved with short completions. Current work (ENG-314159 and ENG-42190) provides instrumentation and prefill telemetry; this ticket builds a runtime decision layer that learns per-trajectory tradeoffs with safety constraints.
proposal: Build a Trajectory Optimizer service inside the runtime scheduler that: 1) issues microprobes for a tiny subset of requests (shadow runs or sampled microbenchmarks) to estimate warmup/gap overheads for candidate kernels; 2) maintains a compact online cost model combining occupancy, kernel latency, warm-gap penalty, and per-token throughput; 3) selects kernel+opvariant per-request with constraint enforcement (latency SLO, cost budget); 4) supports prefill-aware decisions that treat prefill and decode phases differently and can pin a kernel for decode if warm-cache benefit is large.
technical_notes:
- Microprobes: use 1-2 token synthetic shadow calls or cached microbench to estimate kernel startup and KV cache penalty. Limit overhead to <0.1% of requests.
- Cost model: linear regression with recent-window smoothing + Bayesian uncertainty to drive exploration.
- Exploration policy: constrained Thompson Sampling with a safety band (reject actions likely to violate 95th perc SLO).
- Prefill/decode scheduling: token-phase detector marks request as prefill-heavy vs streaming; optimizer can choose fast-prefill-optimized kernels or decode-optimized kernels.
- Warm-gap penalty: model explicitly the cost of switching kernels mid-request (cache invalidation, shader JIT, memory layout change).
- Telemetry: emit per-request decision, expected vs observed cost, and a small fingerprint for arch/seqlen/occupancy for downstream analysis.
milestones:
1) Proto design and API (by 2025-01-22)
2) Microprobe harness + low-overhead sampling (by 2025-01-31)
3) Online cost model + constrained sampler (by 2025-02-10)
4) Prefill/decode phase handling and pinning policy (by 2025-02-17)
5) Internal canary rollout and evaluation (by 2025-02-24)
6) Docs + runbook + perf dashboard (by 2025-02-28)
acceptance_criteria:
- Production canary shows >=10% reduction in 95th-tail latency for mixed workloads versus current heuristics, measured on benchmark harness.
- Average per-token cost does not increase >2% (or shows net improvement) across representative customers.
- No QoE regressions on held-out prompt-set (automated eval pass).
- Observability: per-route decision traces enabled and dashboard with expected vs observed cost.
- Feature guarded behind runtime flag and rollout policy; ability to rollback to static heuristic instantly.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for microprobe sampling and cost-model update code.
- Integration tests: simulated cluster with A100/4090/MI300 images and synthetic sequences to validate decision correctness.
- Performance tests: run full inference harness comparing baseline vs Trajectory Optimizer at 0.1% sampling, 1% sampling, and 5% sampling; measure throughput, tail latency, and overhead.
- Ablation tests: disable warm-gap penalty and observe regression; disable phase-aware pinning and measure impact.
rollout_plan:
- Deploy under feature flag in a single canary region on dedicated capacity nodes.
- Start with sampling rate = 0.1% microprobes for 48h. If safe, increase to 1% and enable constrained exploration.
- Monitor latency SLOs and risk signals for 72h before expanding to other regions.
- Provide one-click rollback to static kernel selector; emergency kill switch at load-balancer level.
notes:
- Stay conservative on exploration early; tail regressions are customer-visible.
- Consider integrating with existing kernel confidence estimator (ENG-______ placeholder) as a downstream consumer.
- Evaluate whether microprobes should be synthetic short-token runs or replays of sampled real requests depending on overhead and privacy constraints.
- Keep privacy: microprobes must not log request payloads; only fingerprint and timing.
risks:
- Microprobe overhead might amplify under high qps if not throttled.
- Warm-gap penalty misestimation could lead to thrashing between kernels.
- Complexity of constrained exploration may delay implementation.
- Edge cases: deterministic pinned kernels for long-running streaming clients conflict with dynamic switching.
followups:
- If successful, schedule follow-up to expose per-tenant cost-control knobs (rate limit exploration per customer) and dashboarding for customers to opt-in.
- Research idea: joint optimization that considers downstream cost of re-ranking or eval steps (cross-service trajectory planning).
